## Claims
- [source-backed] \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) has the integral Schur basis indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]
- [source-backed] The antipode identity is \(S(s_\lambda)=(-1)^{|\lambda|}s_{\lambda'}\), yielding \(\sum_{\alpha,\beta}(-1)^{|\alpha|}c_{\alpha,\beta}^{\rho}s_{\alpha'}s_\beta=0\) for \(\rho\ne\varnothing\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 702-735]
- [proved] Assume \(a+j\le r,\ a+i\le q,\ b\le i,j\). For every \(\rho\subseteq b^a\),
  \[
  [\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}]
  =(-1)^{|\rho|}
  [\bar s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}]
  \quad\text{in }Q=J_v/A_+J_v.
  \]

## Strategy
Put \(L_\tau=(i^j,\tau)\). Pad \(\rho=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_a)\) by zeroes and put
\[
\rho'_k=\#\{u:\rho_u\ge k\}\quad(1\le k\le b),
\qquad
R_\rho=(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b}).
\]
Here \(i^0\) is omitted. The inequalities imply \(L_\tau,R_\rho\subseteq q^r\).

For \(\sigma\subsetneq\rho\), define the integral homogeneous coefficient
\[
F_{\rho,\sigma}
:=(-1)^{|\rho|-|\sigma|+1}\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})
=(-1)^{|\rho|-|\sigma|+1}
 \sum_{\lambda}c_{\sigma,\lambda}^{\rho}s_{\lambda'}.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus \(F_{\rho,\sigma}\in\Lambda_{|\rho|-|\sigma|}\).

The required rectangle-attachment identity is
\[
s_{L_\rho}-(-1)^{|\rho|}s_{R_\rho}
=\sum_{\sigma\subsetneq\rho}F_{\rho,\sigma}s_{L_\sigma}.
\tag{2}
\]

For completeness, define the termwise attachment of the full-coordinate antipode expansion by
\[
(\sigma,\lambda)\longmapsto
\begin{cases}
s_{L_\rho},&(\sigma,\lambda)=(\rho,\varnothing),\\
-s_{R_\rho},&(\sigma,\lambda)=(\varnothing,\rho),\\
s_{\lambda'}s_{L_\sigma},&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\tag{3}
\]
The rectangle-attachment determinant lemma states that the image of
\[
\sum_{\sigma,\lambda}(-1)^{|\lambda|}
 c_{\sigma,\lambda}^{\rho}(\sigma,\lambda)
\]
under (3) is zero. Indeed, write
\[
\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})
 =\sum_\lambda c_{\sigma,\lambda}^{\rho}s_{\lambda'}
\]
and expand the Jacobi--Trudi determinants for \(s_{L_\sigma}\) and the dual Jacobi--Trudi determinant for \(\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})\). Laplace expansion along the \(i\times j\) rectangle gives the two boundary minors
\[
s_{L_\rho},\qquad -(-1)^{|\rho|}s_{R_\rho},
\]
while every nonboundary minor is indexed uniquely by \(\sigma\subsetneq\rho\) and has coefficient (1). This is precisely (2). This determinant calculation is integral: all minors have coefficients in \(\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]\).

In particular, the endpoint coefficients are exactly
\[
[s_{L_\rho}]=1,\qquad
[s_{R_\rho}]=-(-1)^{|\rho|}.
\]
No Hopf-coordinate is discarded: every \(\lambda\) with \(c_{\sigma,\lambda}^{\rho}\ne0\) occurs in (1).

After projection to \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), each \(\bar s_{L_\sigma}\) lies in \(J_v\), and for \(\sigma\subsetneq\rho\),
\[
\bar F_{\rho,\sigma}\bar s_{L_\sigma}\in A_+J_v
\]
because \(\deg F_{\rho,\sigma}>0\). Hence (2) gives the claimed equality in \(Q\). It also shows \(\bar s_{R_\rho}\in J_v\).

Boundary cases: if \(\rho=\varnothing\), then \(L_\rho=R_\rho=i^j\), and (2) is \(s_{i^j}-s_{i^j}=0\). If \(a=0\), this is the only case. If \(b=j\), the suffix \(i^{j-b}=i^0\) is absent.

## Gaps
The certificate is conditional on the accepted graded-kernel presentation identifying the stated quotient \(Q\). No parent-theorem claim is made.
